name: Warm Paper Grid Documentary Background
use_when: A documentary explainer needs an editorial graphic background behind maps, charts, documents, or title text.
A flat color background feels too digital and the section needs analog paper texture.
A sequence needs consistent style across several infographic scenes.
avoid_when: Live footage, source documents, or map detail should fill the frame without extra texture.
The paper or grid texture reduces foreground text, chart, map, or caption readability.
The style would imply a copied publisher identity rather than a project-specific editorial look.

timeline_pattern.canvas_rule: Set the canvas to the intended delivery aspect before scaling the paper background.
timeline_pattern.texture_rule: Texture should give depth, not become the subject.
timeline_pattern.palette_rule: Use warm off-white, charcoal/gray, yellow, red, and muted accents only when they preserve contrast.

motion.rule: Background motion should be minimal; let foreground maps, charts, and text carry the movement.

keyframe_values.paper_scale_start: Scale paper slightly above frame bounds; 115-120% is a useful starting range for 16:9 if edges show.
keyframe_values.grid_opacity: Start around 10-20% opacity so grid structure is visible but subordinate.
keyframe_values.paper_edge_opacity: Start around 15-25% opacity for edge/doodle texture.
keyframe_values.texture_effect: Use subtle hand-drawn or paper-edge motion only after readability is checked.

sound.rule: Background texture alone needs no SFX; save sounds for foreground reveals, highlights, and transitions.

captions.rule: Captions or labels must stay readable over the paper and grid at delivery size.

color.rule: Warm the background slightly without turning it orange or lowering contrast for foreground text.
color.avoid: Avoid saturated paper colors that fight data, maps, or callouts.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use a paper image/video as the base, scale/crop to canvas, apply mild color temperature adjustment, overlay a grid with alpha, and render stills to check text contrast.
implementation.remotion: Create a PaperGridBackground component with paperAsset, scale, warmth, gridOpacity, edgeTextureOpacity, and palette props.
implementation.blender: Use textured planes or compositor overlays for paper and grid, keeping foreground text/material contrast high.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Set ratio, place paper background, scale to cover, warm via Adjustment/Basic temperature, chroma-key or blend the grid layer, and lower opacity around 15%.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use a paper texture layer, Lumetri temperature, grid overlay with blend/opacity, and a nested sequence or Essential Graphics background preset.

common_mistakes: Letting grid lines compete with chart bars, map lines, or small text.
Using a paper texture so strong it looks dirty after compression.
Changing background warmth between scenes without a style reason.
Adding motion texture before checking the foreground layout.
Copying another publisher's exact background identity rather than making a project-specific variant.
qc: Does foreground text, chart data, and map detail remain readable over the background?
Is the grid opacity low enough to feel structural rather than distracting?
Does the warm paper look fit the project tone without becoming orange or muddy?
Are paper edges or doodle textures subordinate and compression-clean?
Is the background legally sourced or generated with manifest/source notes when used in a project?
